corrected_draft.description_short: Executive Order 13780 imposed temporary entry restrictions on nationals of six countries and paused refugee admissions in 2017.
corrected_draft.description_medium: President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780 on March 6, 2017, revising his earlier travel restrictions. The order set a 90-day entry suspension for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to exceptions, and a separate 120-day pause on refugee admissions. It omitted Iraq from the six-country list. Federal courts issued separate injunctions against provisions before the order’s scheduled effective date; later appellate rulings addressed the Hawaii and Maryland cases separately.
corrected_draft.description_long: On March 6, 2017, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13780, “Protecting the Nation from Foreign Terrorist Entry into the United States,” replacing his January order. The Federal Register text set a 90-day entry suspension for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria and Yemen, subject to stated exceptions, and a separate 120-day pause on refugee admissions. Iraq was no longer on the covered-country list. The order stated an effective time of March 16, 2017. A federal court in Hawaii and a separate court in Maryland enjoined different provisions before that date. The White House later described the injunctions as distinct: Maryland’s order concerned section 2(c), while the Ninth Circuit affirmed portions of the Hawaii injunction affecting sections 2 and 6. These records support a concise account of the order and separate litigation. They do not support compressing the cases into one injunction or saying both appellate courts upheld the same claims. The original Associated Press link concerned Trump tweets and votes and was unrelated to Executive Order 13780. This revision cites the order, the Ninth Circuit opinion and the administration’s memorandum about the separate injunctions, while preserving the procedural distinctions.
